title: Product Test Applicability
purpose: Defines the governed applicability state used to determine whether generic product implementation tests are expected for a repository state and whether zero applicable tests is legitimate.

normative_requirements.text: The product shall define `product-test-applicability` as the governed repository-state determination of which product implementation-test obligations are applicable to `product/scripts/test-product`.
Product-test applicability shall be derived from accepted repository-local product authority and test obligation evidence, not inferred solely from the presence or absence of discovered test files.

A repository may have a legitimate zero-applicable product-test state only when accepted repository-local authority establishes that no governed product implementation-test obligation applies to the current repository state.

Legitimate zero-applicable state shall be represented by deterministic evidence sufficient to distinguish intentional absence of governed product implementation tests from accidental absence, missing registration, broken discovery, or incomplete installation.

If accepted repository-local authority establishes that one or more governed product implementation-test obligations apply, failure to resolve all expected applicable obligations shall not be classified as zero applicable.

The applicability state shall distinguish at minimum: zero-applicable, applicable-and-resolved, and applicability-invalid. Applicability-invalid shall include contradictory, incomplete, malformed, or otherwise insufficient governing evidence.
Applicability-invalid shall fail closed and shall not be normalized to zero-applicable or successful product testing.

Transition from zero-applicable to applicable product tests shall occur through governed repository authority that establishes one or more applicable product-test obligations; the stable `product/scripts/test-product` interface identity shall not change as a consequence of that transition.

This applicability contract shall not prescribe a registry file format, discovery path layout, activation trigger representation, product-specific test semantics, test framework, or exact user-facing wording.
